notes: Read the complete small-business target, full preceding labor context, all twelve candidates and the review. Restored U.S. scope to the jobs figures and classified reported Obama and Democratic actions and claimed effects as factual assertions rather than prospective positions. Named President Obama where the model left President unresolved. Identified the employer health-insurance tax credit and split its predicted 2014 growth from the separate purchasing-pool mechanism.

claims.claim_text: Over the preceding two decades, U.S. small businesses created two of every three net new jobs.
President Obama signed eighteen small-business tax cuts intended to encourage hiring and job-creating machinery and equipment investment.
President Obama proposed significant additional small-business tax relief.
President Obama encouraged investment and supported start-ups by allowing businesses to deduct the full cost of new equipment and machinery purchased in 2011.
President Obama's Small Business Jobs Act accelerated $55 billion in tax relief through 2011.
Democrats made loans needed for growth and hiring easier for small businesses to obtain.
President Obama signed changes intended to help entrepreneurs raise capital while maintaining key investor protections.
U.S. small businesses had resumed creating jobs.
Democrats used an employer health-insurance tax credit to help small businesses provide health coverage to workers.
In 2014, the small-business employer health-insurance tax credit would increase.
In 2014, small businesses would be able to pool purchasing power to obtain affordable health coverage.
